summary: Replace the current flat-rate, double-counting recommendation engine with a rigorous, auditable system. Key changes: (1) category-specific savings rates sourced from a new reference YAML rather than a single global config value, (2) an explicit addressability percentage per lever x category that reduces the baseline to account for locked-in or unaddressable spend, (3) a SpendAllocator that prevents two recommendations from claiming the same spend pool in their impact calculations, (4) four new audit-trail fields on every recommendation dict so analysts can trace exactly how each number was derived, and (5) a portfolio sanity check that flags implausibly high total savings. The dashboard detail cards are updated to display the new fields.

decisions.savings_rates_reference_file: New data/reference/savings_rates.yaml holds per-lever x L1-category rates. Rates fall back to a 'default' entry when a category is not explicitly listed. This makes rates transparent, version-controlled, and editable without touching Python code.
decisions.addressability_applied_in_rules: Each rule computes addressable_baseline = baseline_spend * addressability_pct before applying saving_pct. This isolates the addressability assumption close to where it is used rather than as a post-processing step.
decisions.deduplication_via_spend_allocator: SpendAllocator in deduplicator.py tracks spend claimed per (category_l1, exclusive_group). SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION and COMPETITIVE_TENDER share exclusive_group='SOURCING' — logically mutually exclusive by supplier count but allocator enforces it defensively. CONTRACT_COVERAGE_GAP is group='COVERAGE'. PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION is group='WORKING_CAPITAL'. TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION and CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE are portfolio-level and do not consume category spend pools.
decisions.audit_trail_fields: Add baseline_spend, addressability_pct, saving_pct, addressable_baseline to every recommendation dict. These are display-only and do not affect engine logic. They surface the calculation transparently in the dashboard.
decisions.sanity_threshold_20pct: Engine emits a WARNING log and sets portfolio_summary.sanity_check_passed=False when sum(estimated_impact_aud) / total_spend > 0.20. This is a guard, not a hard cap — the analyst reviews flagged outputs.
decisions.wrapped_json_export: export() writes a wrapper object: {'recommendations': [...], 'portfolio_summary': {...}} rather than a bare list. _load_recommendations() in the dashboard handles both formats for backwards compatibility.
decisions.config_addressability_defaults: RecommendationsConfig gains addressability_defaults dict keyed by lever type plus competitive_tender_min_spend and contract_coverage_gap_min_spend to replace hardcoded thresholds in rules.py.

existing_tables.transactions: Parquet at data/output/transactions.parquet — key columns: base_amount, category_l1, category_l2, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, payment_terms_days, is_intercompany, is_tax_line, po_number, is_on_contract

userStories.title: Create savings_rates.yaml reference file
userStories.description: Create data/reference/savings_rates.yaml containing per-lever savings rates and addressability percentages. The file has two top-level keys: 'defaults' (one entry per lever type as fallback) and 'categories' (L1 category overrides). Each entry has saving_pct (float 0-1) and addressability_pct (float 0-1). Lever type keys must exactly match the constants in src/recommendations/rules.py: SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION, PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION, TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION, CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE, COMPETITIVE_TENDER, CONTRACT_COVERAGE_GAP. Default values: SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION saving_pct=0.08 addressability_pct=0.70; COMPETITIVE_TENDER saving_pct=0.07 addressability_pct=0.65; CONTRACT_COVERAGE_GAP saving_pct=0.05 addressability_pct=0.80; TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION saving_pct=0.10 addressability_pct=0.50; CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE saving_pct=0.05 addressability_pct=0.75; PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION has no saving_pct (uses WACC formula) so omit saving_pct and set addressability_pct=0.80. Category overrides for: 'Information Technology' (SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION: saving_pct=0.12 addressability_pct=0.65; COMPETITIVE_TENDER: saving_pct=0.10 addressability_pct=0.60), 'Professional Services' (SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION: saving_pct=0.10 addressability_pct=0.55; COMPETITIVE_TENDER: saving_pct=0.08 addressability_pct=0.50), 'Facilities Management' (SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION: saving_pct=0.07 addressability_pct=0.72), 'Marketing and Communications' (SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION: saving_pct=0.12 addressability_pct=0.60), 'Logistics and Transport' (COMPETITIVE_TENDER: saving_pct=0.09 addressability_pct=0.70).

userStories.title: Create SpendAllocator deduplication module
userStories.description: Create src/recommendations/deduplicator.py containing a SpendAllocator class that prevents two recommendations from double-counting the same spend pool. EXCLUSIVE_GROUPS mapping at module level: {'SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION': 'SOURCING', 'COMPETITIVE_TENDER': 'SOURCING', 'CONTRACT_COVERAGE_GAP': 'COVERAGE', 'PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION': 'WORKING_CAPITAL', 'TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION': 'PORTFOLIO_TAIL', 'CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE': 'PORTFOLIO_COMPLIANCE'}. SpendAllocator.allocate(recommendations: list[dict]) -> list[dict]: (1) Sort input by estimated_impact_aud descending. (2) For each rec, compute pool_key: for PORTFOLIO_* groups use ('PORTFOLIO', exclusive_group); for all others use (rec['context'], exclusive_group). (3) If pool_key is already in claimed set: set rec['estimated_impact_aud'] = 0.0, set rec['deduplication_note'] = 'Spend pool already claimed by higher-impact recommendation of same exclusive group'. (4) Else: add pool_key to claimed set. (5) After processing all recs, filter out those where estimated_impact_aud == 0.0. (6) Return filtered list. Work on a deep copy of the input list to avoid mutating callers' data.

userStories.title: Wire SpendAllocator and portfolio summary into engine.py
userStories.description: Update src/recommendations/engine.py to run SpendAllocator deduplication and add a portfolio sanity check with wrapped JSON export. Read the full file before making changes. In RecommendationEngine.run(): after rules.generate_all() and before narrative enrichment, call deduplicated = SpendAllocator().allocate(recommendations) (import SpendAllocator from src.recommendations.deduplicator). After deduplication, compute total_savings = sum(r['estimated_impact_aud'] for r in deduplicated) and total_spend = metrics.get('total_spend', 0.0). Compute savings_pct = total_savings / total_spend if total_spend > 0 else 0.0. If savings_pct > 0.20, log WARNING and set sanity_passed = False, else True. Store self._portfolio_summary = {'total_spend': round(total_spend,2), 'total_identified_savings': round(total_savings,2), 'savings_as_pct_of_spend': round(savings_pct,4), 'sanity_check_passed': sanity_passed, 'recommendation_count': len(deduplicated)} as an instance variable for use by export(). In export(): write {'recommendations': recommendations, 'portfolio_summary': self._portfolio_summary} instead of bare list. Initialise self._portfolio_summary = {} in __init__. Also update dashboard/pages/06_recommendations.py: in _load_recommendations(), if the loaded JSON is a dict with 'recommendations' key, return data['recommendations']; else return data as-is (backwards compat). Add a new @st.cache_data function _load_portfolio_summary() that reads the same file and returns data.get('portfolio_summary', {}) if dict, else {}.
